PIVOTED TO EVOFORMER TTT: ESMFold TTT showed negligible improvement (folding head bottleneck). Now applying ProteinTTT to AlphaFold-Multimer's Evoformer backbone — the head IS competent for complexes. OpenFold v2.2.0 installed with multimer support. 288 LoRA targets (MSA row+column attention Q/K/V). 1.18M trainable params. Pilot running on TITAN RTX. Generating ColabFold MSAs for DB5.5 pairs (single-sequence AF2-Multimer gives degenerate predictions).

KEY INSIGHT: ESMFold negative + Evoformer positive = strong mechanistic argument. TTT works when the downstream head is competent for the task, fails when it isn't. This is the core story for the paper.

PRELIMINARY FINDINGS (46/183 uniform, 13/183 cross-chain/interface): TTT reduces MLM perplexity (loss 2.5→0.6) but DockQ improvements are NEGLIGIBLE (<0.001). Baseline ESMFold+linker gets 16.4% success. TTT finds different confidence-optimal steps ~50% of cases but these do not translate to DockQ improvement. Key insight: folding trunk (not trained for complexes) is the bottleneck, not the language model representations. This is an important negative result showing representation-level adaptation cannot compensate for architectural limitations in multi-chain prediction.

FULL BASELINE COMPLETE (183 pairs, V100): mean DockQ=0.126, success=16.4% (30/183), medium=12.6%, high=4.9%. Top: 3SZK(0.968), 1YVB(0.955), 1XU1(0.941). TTT experiments running on V100: 13/183 pairs done per strategy (~1.75h elapsed). TTT finds non-baseline best steps in ~50% of cases. 4 rounds of continuation jobs queued to process all 183 pairs per strategy.
